note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart. Claims about the world, such as how many courts a venue has and what it costs, come from the City of St. George and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Washington County. This is the first county in Utah this directory has published in, and one city of it is on this page.

slots.coverage:
One city in Washington County is published here: St. George, with three venues and forty-six courts checked against the City's own pickleball page. Washington County also contains Washington City, Hurricane, Santa Clara and Ivins, and the County itself runs parks. None of those operators has been read, so none appears here.

The page that has been read gives St. George's inventory in four lines: Little Valley with thirty-three courts, Bloomington Park with seven, Vernon Worthen with six, and Ledges with four and a question mark where its address should be. The first three publish. Ledges does not, because a venue needs a street address that resolves and the City has printed "?" in its place. St. George is the first Utah city on this site, and Little Valley's thirty-three ties Albuquerque's Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex as the largest single venue anywhere here.
slots.distribution:
What we cover in this county sits in one city, and within that city it sits mostly in one place. Thirty-three of the forty-six published courts are at Little Valley Pickleball Complex on Horseman Park Drive, which is the City's programmed facility: a numbered court plan, a 2025 schedule of leagues, youth sessions, clinics and tournaments with courts reserved for each, an attendant to check in with, and a court-reservation line at the Parks Department.

The remaining thirteen are in two parks: seven at Bloomington Park on Man O War Road in the south-west of the city, and six at Vernon Worthen Park at 300 S. 400 E. near the centre. The City states nothing about either beyond a name, an address and a count.

Lighting is not stated anywhere in the county's published record, and neither is surface, hours, or whether any court is indoor. Price is stated once: Little Valley's courts are free of charge when vacant, in the City's own 2020 words, and the other two venues carry no price at all.
slots.gaps:
This is a St. George page under the heading of a county. Washington City, Hurricane, Santa Clara and Ivins have not been read, and neither has Washington County's own parks department.

Inside St. George the gap is narrower and stranger. The City has stated fifty courts and forty-six can be published, and the missing four are missing for a punctuation mark: "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4". Nothing about those courts being real is in doubt; the City simply has not written down where they are.

The other gap is inside the published record. The City's page is a programme page, built to tell league players when their courts are reserved, and it is silent on almost everything a first-time visitor would ask: lighting at every venue, surface at every venue, opening hours at every venue, parking, restrooms, and price at two venues out of three. Whatever pickleball exists in the county at schools, clubs or private communities has published no source that could be read.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Washington County?
faqs.a: Nobody knows the whole number. What has been checked is 46 courts across three venues, all in St. George, each with a source and a date you can see. The City of St. George itself states fifty, the extra four being at Ledges, which it lists without an address.

The City of St. George's pickleball complex at 2149 Horseman Park Drive, with thirty-three courts on the City's current list, a published programme schedule, an attendant, and free play when courts are vacant. It ties Albuquerque's Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex as the largest single venue on this site.

faqs.q: Are the courts on this page free?
faqs.a: Stated at one venue only. The City's 2020 article says of Little Valley that "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge". Vernon Worthen Park and Bloomington Park carry no price either way, so they are recorded as unknown.

None that the City states. Its pickleball page never mentions lighting at any venue, so every court in this county is recorded as lighting not stated. Little Valley's schedule runs evening sessions to 9:30 p.m. in winter, which is a timetable fact and not a lighting answer.

faqs.q: Why does Little Valley show 33 courts when the City's article says 24?
faqs.a: Because the two figures are different kinds of record. The article is dated 19 August 2020 and describes the complex as it was then; the court list is the City's undated present inventory. A dated history does not contradict a current list, so thirty-three publishes and twenty-four is printed as what the venue was.

sources.evidence: The City's Pickleball page. Under "City of St. George Pickleball Courts" exactly four lines: "Little Valley / 2149 Horseman Park Drive / Courts:  33", "Vernon Worthen / 300 S. 400 E. / Courts: 6", "Bloomington Park / 650 Man O War Road / Courts: 7", "Ledges / ? / Courts: 4". The "St. George Pickleball Program Schedule / 2025" for Little Valley, reserving "9-32 (24 courts)" for league sessions and "All 33 Courts" for two tournaments; "Players, please check in with the attendant or instructor to determine if courts are available during the St. George Pickleball programs"; "Please contact Parks to make a court reservation at 435-627-4530". The article dated "St. George, UT, August 19, 2020": "The Little Valley Pickleball complex is home to 24 well-maintained courts." and "When courts are vacant the public readily takes advantage of them - free of charge."
